subject: Testcase conveyance — MAP closewalk & acceptance runway
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@quantaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Testcase conveyance — MAP closewalk & acceptance runway

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (QuantaRetail_MAP_v1.pdf) and a short sample promptpack we can provide as read-only to validate runner compatibility. High level proposal:

- Mutual Action Plan milestone 1: Provide initial testcase CSV & promptpack to your sandbox (ephemeral access) — target: 2027-09-29
- Milestone 2: Acceptance window (canary evaluation) — 3 business days after ingestion
- Milestone 3: Sign-off & billing start — target close: 2027-10-08

Usage constraints we need agreed up front (we can be flexible but need them codified):
- Ephemeral sandbox only: no long-term retention of raw testcases on Quanta side unless agreed
- Promptpack access: read-only, no redistribution beyond the evaluation team
- Token limits for acceptance runs: 200k tokens total for the canary window unless extended by mutual consent

Please review the attached MAP and the small promptpack we included (promptpack_sample_v2.zip). If that looks ok, can we get procurement looped and a preferred close date? If you want us to redact or provide a pseudonymized CSV, we can do that — we just need to know PII expectations.

Talk soon — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to lock dates.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the plan and the attachments. Quick notes from our side:

- Procurement will need a short SOW and an MPA template we can sign. I copied procurement and Charles — they'll own the contract cadence.
- Security ask: the evaluation must be done in an ephemeral sandbox; Quanta policy forbids retention of raw customer testcases in production stores. Can Redwood support a wipe-after-evaluation workflow?
- We will supply an initial set of testcases (CSV) but need to keep them within our legal team until we have an NDA addendum signed.

Our internal target would be to have the evaluation kickoff by 2027-09-30 if possible. Can you confirm you can deliver the ingestion artifacts and the canary/acceptance criteria by 09/29?

Also attaching our procurement intake form separately (we will upload to your S3 link).

Best,
Emma Hughes
Director of Product QA, QuantaRetail
emma.hughes@quantaretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@quantaretail.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Testcase conveyance — MAP closewalk & acceptance runway

Emma —

Appreciate the heads up. Quick confirmations from Redwood (high level) so procurement/security have concrete items to review: 

1) Data handling & retention
- We can support ephemeral sandboxes with an automated wipe at the end of the acceptance window. We'll provide a wipe proof log (hash of deletion job) to Quanta's security contact.

2) Testcase delivery and format
- Preferred: CSV with columns [id, prompt, expected_output_category, complexity_tag]. We can accept up to ~10k lines for the initial canary; if you need more we will stage in batches.

3) Usage constraints (required in MPA)
- Read-only promptpack distribution; no redistribution outside Quanta evaluation team
- No retention beyond the agreed teardown date (we'll run the deletion job within 48 hours after acceptance window unless extended)
- Token cap for canary evaluation: 200k tokens total; any overage requires pre-approval or will be billed per standard overage rates

4) Acceptance criteria (suggestion)
- Functional: pass rate >= 85% for the defined expected_output_category mapping for intent-level tests
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 350ms on standard requests during canary

Attachments: redwood-usage-constraints.pdf (details + example manifest). Also attaching a short ingestion checklist we use internally.

If Quanta confirms the CSV format and the sandbox wipe requirement, we can proceed to publish the ingestion lane and create a short DocuSign MPA that matches these bullets.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-usage-constraints.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]

Emma / Procurement —

Thanks — based on the thread below here's the agreed closewalk and next steps. Please reply with any change requests; otherwise we'll kick off per this timeline.

Milestones (final):
- 2027-09-29: Quanta uploads testcases_initial.csv to our access-controlled bucket (s3 link above). Please confirm upload and PII preference (mask/remove).
- 2027-09-29 17:00 PT: Redwood publishes ingestion manifest and promptpack (read-only) to the evaluation lane.
- 2027-09-30 — 2027-10-04: Canary acceptance window (3 business days). Acceptance criteria per Marissa (>=85% functional pass, p95 <350ms).
- 2027-10-06: Final sign-off meeting and close; billing start date 2027-10-08 if sign-off achieved.

Docs & links:
- DocuSign MPA draft: https://docusign.com/MT-QR-2027-0924
- HubSpot deal: https://redwood.app/hubspot/deal/QR-2027-09-24-01
- Ingestion bucket: s3://redwood-secure/quantaretail/provisioning/

Attachments included with this email: mutual-action-timeline.xlsx (milestone tracker), testcases_initial.csv (sample skeleton), and the final promptpack we will instantiate for the canary.

If Quanta procurement can sign the DocuSign MPA by 09/30 morning and upload the CSV by 09/29 EOD PT, we will meet the 10/06 sign-off target. If timeline slips we will publish a new runway date.

Thanks all — I will schedule a 20-min kickoff for 2027-09-29 10:00 PT and send calendar invites after procurement confirms.

Regards,
